findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Correct edit #3's premise: `pass_id` is NOT delivered to `_apply_outbound_update` via `**_kwargs` (typed_dispatch.py `_apply_typed` passes only client/repo_root/binding_store) — add threading `pass_id` through `_apply_typed` and the outbound leaf signature to the scope, or source `confirmed_pass` another way.
evidence: Plan: '_apply_outbound_update ... already receives binding_store / repo_root / pass_id through **_kwargs; name them explicitly.'
typed_dispatch.py:137-142 builds _leaf_kwargs with only client, repo_root, binding_store — no pass_id key
Repo-wide grep for `pass_id` in rebar_reconciler shows it threaded through reconcile/applier/differ/apply_handlers (ctx.pass_id) but NEVER into the typed outbound leaves
AC3 requires the written record carry 'the pass_id', and the record()/callback API takes pass_id
findings.finding: Edit #3 asserts `_apply_outbound_update` already receives `pass_id` through `**_kwargs`, but the sole dispatcher `_apply_typed` (typed_dispatch.py:94-142) threads only `client`, `repo_root`, and `binding_store` into leaves — `pass_id` is never passed to the outbound apply leaves. `binding_store`/`repo_root` are available (verified), but `pass_id` is not, so the callback the edit builds has no `pass_id` source for the `confirmed_pass` field AC3 requires.
scenarios: Wiring the link_confirm callback in _apply_outbound_update: pass_id is unresolved, so confirmed_pass cannot be populated
AC3 test asserts the record's confirmed_pass equals the dispatched pass_id
findings.suggested_fix: Extend `_apply_typed` (typed_dispatch.py) to inspect for and forward `pass_id` alongside `binding_store`/`repo_root`, and have its caller supply the pass's id; then name `pass_id` explicitly in `_apply_outbound_update`. Keep the parameter optional so leaves that don't declare it are unaffected.

evidence: Plan: 'It already receives binding_store / repo_root / pass_id through **_kwargs; name them explicitly.'
typed_dispatch.py:137-141 builds _leaf_kwargs = {'client': client}; adds repo_root if accepted; adds binding_store if accepted — there is no pass_id branch.
AC3 requires the record to carry 'the pass_id', so a real source for pass_id is load-bearing.
findings.finding: The plan claims _apply_outbound_update 'already receives binding_store / repo_root / pass_id through **_kwargs', but the typed dispatcher _apply_typed never passes pass_id to any leaf — it threads only client, repo_root, and binding_store.
scenarios: Building the link_confirm callback in _apply_outbound_update and reading pass_id from **_kwargs — it is absent, so pass_id is None/KeyError.
findings.suggested_fix: Add pass_id to _apply_typed's leaf-kwargs plumbing (and its applier.py call sites) analogous to binding_store, or source pass_id from another available context; update the write-seam edit list accordingly.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Resolve which update_one caller is the production outbound-update path: apply_handlers.py::handle_update (line 211) is a second, unenumerated caller whose docstring in _apply_outbound_update identifies IT as the production path — either build link_confirm there (ctx has binding_store/pass_id/repo_root) or justify why the typed leaf is the production seam.
evidence: Two callers of update_one: apply_outbound.py:159 (typed leaf) and apply_handlers.py:211 (handle_update, batch path).

apply_outbound.py:129-138 docstring: 'Production applies every outbound update via batch_dispatch.update_one (the legacy batch path). This typed leaf used to carry a SECOND, parallel implementation ... That parallel logic is gone. The leaf now converts the Mutation to the batch dict and delegates to update_one.'
handle_update already has ctx.binding_store / ctx.pass_id / ctx.repo_root (BatchApplyContext, apply_handlers.py:78-89).
findings.finding: update_one has a second production caller, apply_handlers.py::handle_update (line 211), which the plan does not name; the typed leaf _apply_outbound_update's own docstring states production applies every outbound update via the legacy batch path — so the link_confirm callback built only in _apply_outbound_update may never fire in production.
findings.location: Scope > Write seam (which caller of update_one builds link_confirm)
scenarios: A production outbound ADD dispatched through the legacy batch path (handle_update) — link_confirm is only wired in the typed leaf, so no confirmation record is written.
findings.suggested_fix: Wire link_confirm at the handle_update call site (apply_handlers.py:211) using ctx.binding_store/ctx.pass_id/ctx.repo_root, or explicitly document that outbound updates route through the typed leaf in production and cover handle_update's counter-parity separately.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Re-target the write-seam caller (edit #3) from the typed leaf _apply_outbound_update to the production outbound-update path apply_handlers.handle_update, so link_confirm actually fires on real passes.
evidence: _apply_outbound_update docstring: 'Production applies every outbound update via batch_dispatch.update_one (the legacy batch path). This typed leaf used to carry a SECOND, parallel implementation ... That parallel logic is gone.'

scenarios: Any real reconcile pass that pushes an outbound link ADD: set_relationship succeeds but no record is written because the callback lives in a leaf the pass never enters.
AC3's unit test invokes _update_one_dispatch_links directly with a stub callback and passes green, masking that production wiring records nothing.
findings.suggested_fix: Build the callback in apply_handlers.handle_update using its BatchApplyContext (which already holds client, repo_root, pass_id, binding_store) and pass it into update_one(...) there; drop the _apply_outbound_update edit or keep it only as a mirrored no-op for the typed-dispatch test path.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Correct the pass_id data-flow claim: pass_id does not reach outbound leaves via **_kwargs; source it from apply_handlers' BatchApplyContext.pass_id (or thread it explicitly) at whatever seam the callback is built.

findings.finding: The plan states _apply_outbound_update 'already receives binding_store / repo_root / pass_id through **_kwargs', but the typed dispatcher forwards only client, repo_root, and binding_store to leaves — pass_id is never threaded into any leaf, so edit #3 cannot obtain pass_id where it claims to.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the failure behavior of the link_confirm callback (record/save raising) at the dispatch call site — must be swallowed/logged without altering _links_applied/_links_computed or dispatch outcome, consistent with fail-open.
evidence: Plan: 'invoke link_confirm(to_key=..., relation=..., link_id=...). The call is inside the existing try, AFTER _links_applied += 1, so a failed set_relationship records nothing.'
The plan specifies fail-open for load/save of the store, but does not specify that a callback/record/save failure must be swallowed or surfaced without affecting dispatch counters.
findings.finding: The write callback (link_confirm -> record/save) is placed inside the existing dispatch try block after `_links_applied += 1`, but the plan never states what happens if the confirmation write itself (record() or save()) raises. Load/save is declared fail-open, yet the callback path's failure handling at the dispatch call site is unspecified — a raised exception could be caught by the surrounding try and either corrupt dispatch flow or violate the AC6 counter-parity guarantee.
findings.location: Scope > Write seam, edit 1: 'The call is inside the existing try, AFTER _links_applied += 1'
scenarios: A save() failure (e.g. transient disk/permission error) during a successful dispatch raises inside the try, potentially masking the successful set_relationship as failed or aborting subsequent dispatch.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a clause: the callback invocation is wrapped so that any exception in record()/save() is logged and swallowed (never re-raised into dispatch), preserving counter parity; add an AC asserting a raising callback does not change _links_applied.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the retirement/cleanup owner for peer_confirmations records (or explicitly note that pruning is deferred to a named story and why unbounded growth is acceptable in the interim).
evidence: Plan: 'Store file: .tickets-tracker/.bridge_state/peer_confirmations.json' with a record per (source_local_id, target_local_id, relation).
Out of scope names S2/S3/S4 but no story is named as owning retirement/cleanup of stale confirmation records.
findings.finding: peer_confirmations.json is new durable shared state keyed per managed link, but the plan defines CREATE/UPDATE/CONSUME with no RETIRE/cleanup path — records accumulate indefinitely and are never removed when a link is legitimately removed or a ticket retired. The plan defers removal to S3 but does not state whether/when confirmation records are pruned.
findings.location: Scope > Store file and Record key; Out of scope
scenarios: Long-lived repos accumulate orphaned confirmation records for links that no longer exist, growing the JSON store unbounded.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a one-line note to Out of scope / Context naming which story (S3 removal or a follow-up) prunes confirmation records for removed links, or justify that per-link records are bounded by live-link count.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Align AC4 wording with Scope edit 2: use `result.get("id")` (returns None on missing) rather than `result["id"]`.
evidence: AC4: 'link_id is taken from set_relationship's returned mapping (result["id"])'
Scope edit 2: 'pass result.get("id") as link_id when the return is a Mapping, else None ... a missing id is recorded as null and is NOT a failure.'
findings.finding: Terminology drift between AC4 and the Scope write-seam on how link_id is extracted: AC4 says `result["id"]` (subscript) while Scope edit 2 says `result.get("id")` when the return is a Mapping. Both intend the same, but the AC's subscript form implies a KeyError on a missing id, which contradicts the body's explicit 'missing id is recorded as null'.
findings.location: AC4 vs Scope > Write seam edit 2
scenarios: An implementer following AC4 literally could use subscript access and raise KeyError when the mapping lacks 'id', violating the body's null-on-missing rule.
findings.suggested_fix: Reword AC4 to 'link_id is taken via result.get("id") from the returned mapping'.

findings.finding: The durability edit under-specifies the second file guard in _commit_binding_store_snapshot: adding peer_confirmations.json to _rel_files alone leaves it out of the _tracked_basenames set (the bug-1e08 per-file idempotency check), so a peer-confirmation-only staged change hits `_tracked_basenames & _staged_basenames` == empty and returns 'nothing to commit', silently dropping the store — the exact b8b1 loss the plan cites.
findings.suggested_fix: Amend the Durability bullet to name both the `_rel_files` list (line 207) and the `_tracked_basenames` set (lines 234-238), plus a new `git_adapter.PEER_CONFIRMATIONS_FILE` constant; AC7 should assert the file both appears staged AND actually commits when it is the only changed file.

findings.finding: The durability inventory for symbol _commit_binding_store_snapshot is incomplete: the plan patches only the _rel_files staging list, but the same function has a SECOND parallel list, _tracked_basenames (reconcile_helpers.py:234), that drives the per-file idempotency check at line 240, plus the file path is a git_adapter module constant (git_adapter.py:88, __all__ at line 41) with no plan-named analogue for peer_confirmations.json.
findings.location: Scope → Durability: 'add the new file to the staged `_rel_files` list in `reconcile_helpers.py::_commit_binding_store_snapshot`'
findings.suggested_fix: State three edits, not one: (1) add `PEER_CONFIRMATIONS_FILE = f"{BRIDGE_STATE_DIR}/peer_confirmations.json"` in git_adapter.py and export it in __all__; (2) append git_adapter.PEER_CONFIRMATIONS_FILE to _rel_files; (3) append its basename to _tracked_basenames so the bug-1e08 per-file idempotency check does not skip a peer-confirmations-only commit.

findings.finding: The plan asserts 'no key translation is needed' at the write site, but the record key (source_local_id, target_local_id, relation) needs LOCAL ids while the outbound ADD entry carries only Jira keys (issue_key as source, entry['to_key'] as target); the target local id requires a binding_store.get_local_id(to_key) reverse-map, and _update_one_dispatch_links (and update_one) receive no binding_store today.
findings.location: Scope → 'Write site' bullet ('The outbound ADD payload already carries relation, so no key translation is needed'); AC3
findings.suggested_fix: Pass the binding_store through update_one to _update_one_dispatch_links; build the key as (mutation['local_id'], binding_store.get_local_id(entry['to_key']), entry['relation']); when the target reverse-map returns None, skip recording (unbound target, retry next pass) rather than writing a Jira-key-shaped key.

findings.finding: The record field link_id ('vendor link id when the transport supplies one, else null') has no stated source: set_relationship returns dict[str, Any] but the current dispatch call discards the return value.

The write-site plumbing is unenumerated: `_update_one_dispatch_links(mutation, client, issue_key)` returns tuple[int,int] and has no `pass_id` parameter nor a peer_confirmations store handle, yet the plan requires recording `pass_id` and calling `record(...)` there. The signature change and its sole caller (dispatch_one.py line 454) are not called out.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to the Write site bullet: thread the open store and pass_id as new keyword args into `_update_one_dispatch_links` and update its caller at dispatch_one.py:454; note both edits are in-dir and additive.
